quotes.text: Reactive FinOps fails because it still assumes reporting is control. It isn't. What most teams do is simple enough. They observe spend, build reports, explain variances, raise questions and then try to clean things up after the fact.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the core flaw of reactive FinOps: treating reporting as if it were control.

quotes.text: Use deny for the things that are never allowed under any circumstances. Use modify where metadata should be inherited or corrected during the request, especially for tags that need to flow down from a resource group.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives concrete guidance on choosing Azure Policy effects for cost control.

quotes.text: When getting an exemption becomes easier than fixing a template, the system teaches people bypass behavior and governance gets hollowed out by convenience.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how unmanaged exemptions quietly erode governance.

quotes.text: So phase two is repair work. Update templates, adjust module defaults, clean up landing zones, add the required tags into the deployment path. If a compliant deployment is harder than a non-compliant one, the rollout is already broken.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for fixing the platform before tightening enforcement.

quotes.text: Clear rules speed delivery. vague freedom slows it down. If engineers know which regions are allowed, which SKUs pass, and which tags are mandatory, they spend less time guessing and less time reworking. What delays teams is not control, it's inconsistent control.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Argues that clear guardrails speed up engineering delivery instead of slowing it.

takeaways: Cost alerts and dashboards provide visibility, but only enforcement at the Azure Resource Manager request path, such as Azure Policy deny effects, actually prevents waste before billing starts.
Encode financial intent as policy: deny high-cost SKUs and regions where they do not belong, use modify to inherit cost tags, and package rules into initiatives assigned through management groups.

Roll out in stages - time-boxed audit, platform and template repair, deny in non-production, then production with owned, expiring exceptions - and measure prevented cost and cost-weighted adherence rather than compliance percentages.
hook: Most FinOps teams still rely on alerts, dashboards and month-end reviews while Azure spend grows in real time. This episode shows cloud platform, governance and FinOps teams how to turn Azure Policy from passive audit mode into a real-time enforcement gate that blocks wasteful deployments before they ever reach the bill.
